messages:
adele: Heads-up — we hit a production hit where requests routed to a replica CMK in another account are failing to decrypt during regional failover. Error from service logs: "AccessDeniedException: Caller is not authorized to use the key" and CloudTrail shows kms:Decrypt denied for arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:888888888888:key/abcd-REPLICA.

maria: ah — are those replica CMKs in a different AWS account? Grants/policies on replica keys don't auto-propagate, afaik. quick check: do we create grants via aws-kms or rely on key policy? :thinking:

sam: Confirming what maria said — multi-Region CMKs (MRK) don't replicate IAM/grant state. You must either: (a) add an explicit key policy in the replica account that allows the caller (role/principal) or (b) create a grant on the replica CMK for the principal. Example grant CLI:

```\naws kms create-grant \
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:888888888888:key/abcd-REPLICA \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::444444444444:role/RedwoodKMSRole \
  --operations Decrypt,Encrypt\n```

kevin: Quick note — if the app uses envelope encryption, the flow is: app requests CMK to Decrypt DEK ciphertext (wrapped DEK) -> CMK returns plaintext DEK -> app uses DEK to decrypt payload. If the CMK call hits a replica in another account and that replica lacks a matching grant/policy, the kms:Decrypt call will fail even though the DEK itself is valid. :exclamation:

adele: That matches what we see. The DEK is the same, we only see AccessDenied on the KMS call. Any tips for auditing to prove it's a policy/grant miss vs something else?

maria: Enable CloudTrail management events for KMS (Encrypt/Decrypt/ReEncrypt/GenerateDataKey) and look at RequestParameters.cmkId and awsAccountId in the event. Also check KMS event's errorCode and errorMessage fields — they usually indicate AccessDenied. For deeper context, capture the ciphertext blob id and map it back to the envelope operation in our logs.

sam: Also dump the key policy and grants from the replica account to compare. Commands:

```\naws kms get-key-policy --key-id <replica-key-id> --policy-name default\naws kms list-grants --key-id <replica-key-id>\n```

kevin: One subtlety — MRKs keep the same KeyId across regions but the ARN includes region/account. If your service stores the MRK ARN for primary and then you attempt decrypt against a replica CMK ARN, make sure the principal you call from matches the grantee in the replica account. Grants are account-scoped.

adele: Good call. We store the MRK alias ARN and our routing switches region+account in failover. It looks like we failed to provision the grant in the replica account when onboarding that tenant.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: New runbook step added to infra/keys: "ensure replica CMKs have explicit grants for cross-account service roles" — https://redwood.internal/runbooks/keys (automated) :robot_face:

maria: About rotation — if we rotate CMKs or rewrap DEKs, be careful: automatic MRK rotation is separate from envelope DEK rotation. If you rewrap a ciphertext with a different CMK (ReEncrypt), you need permissions on both source and destination keys. Example re-encrypt: 

```\naws kms re-encrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin \
  --source-key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:888888888888:key/old \
  --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:888888888888:key/new\n```

sam: For operational failover pattern I recommend this order in client: 1) attempt Decrypt with primary CMK (fast path), 2) on AccessDenied or NotFound try replica CMK(s) in configured order, 3) if decrypt still fails, surface clear error and capture KMS event IDs for triage. Keep retry backoff small to avoid extra billing. Pseudocode: 

```\nfor key in [primary, replica1, replica2]:\n  try:\n    plain_dek = kms.decrypt(ciphertext_blob, key)\n    return use_dek(plain_dek)\n  except KmsAccessDenied:\n    log.warn("kms deny", key=key)\n    continue\nraise DecryptFailed\n```

kevin: Also add a short audit column in our datastore recording which CMK/ARN was used for decrypt attempts (success/fail) so we can quickly correlate to a particular replica/key policy.

adele: Plan: kevin will add grants/policy changes to the replica keys for the tenant account (tracked in #infra-keys), maria will add the CloudTrail + extra logging instrumentation, sam will add the fallback pseudo-code as a safe client change and a feature flag to control failover order. I'll open a follow-up ticket for rotation playbook to ensure re-encrypt/DEK rotation has cross-account permissions. Who wants to own the incident ticket? :raised_hands:

kevin: I'll own the ticket and push the replica grant change. I'll post the grant IDs here when done. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll add the CloudTrail alerts and a Kibana dashboard for kms:Decrypt failures grouped by cmk id. :mag:

sam: I'll draft the client change as a small PR behind a flag. Should be non-disruptive.

adele: Great — thanks. If anyone sees another AccessDenied for a different region/account, ping me directly and include the CloudTrail event id. :eyes:
